question: Does X64 (the 64-token needle distance, held-out segments) keep being learned past update 200, if the run is resumed from the update-200 checkpoint with the same recipe (replay weight 0.25, one global clip at 1.0) for 100 more updates, and does Y72 retention survive?
design: One run, one seed. Resume from the update-200 checkpoint (restored with a zero-tolerance restoration check: model hash and every integer count equal to the pinned update-200 values), extend the pinned data plan to 300 updates (6 X rows + 2 replay rows per update), checkpoint and evaluate at 225/250/275/300, always stop at 300. Pre-registered stop rule (prereg/stop_rule_300.json): STUCK / INCONCLUSIVE, with retention failure reported separately and blocking any success claim.

setup.hardware: one free-tier GPU session, 2 x T4 (training on one device)

final.reading: X64 held-out exact went 0 -> 11 -> 29 -> 46 -> 92 of 240 (held-out rows disjoint from every training row), so X64 was still being learned; Y72 retention fell from 168 at update 225 to 137, 137, 153 at 250/275/300, all below the 160 floor. Retention failure blocks any success claim; the verdict is INCONCLUSIVE.

verdict: INCONCLUSIVE (not stuck; X64 held-out 92/240 at update 300); retention failure at 250, 275, 300 (Y72 137, 137, 153 of 200 vs floor 160)
